claims.text: Academic critiques of the youth social media harm thesis did not increase in volume or literature share after Meta's March 2023 meeting notes.
The critique share of works taking a stance on the harm thesis fell from 24.6% in the 24 months before March 2023 to 16.7% in the 24 months after (odds ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.33 to 1.14).
84.8% of post-March 2023 critiques with usable reference data cite at least one critique published before the notes, compared to 56.1% of post-notes supportive works (odds ratio 4.35, p < 0.001).
29.3% of post-March 2023 critiques share an author with an earlier critique, compared to 17.4% of supportive works sharing an author with an earlier supportive work (odds ratio 1.97, p = 0.046).
No critique in the 2,032-work corpus lists Meta, Facebook, or Instagram as a funder in Crossref metadata.
Only one record in the corpus lists Facebook funder metadata, which is an empirical adolescent mood study coded as neither critique nor supportive.
Later critiques draw on the earlier critical literature in their resolved references at more than twice the rate that later supportive works do (6.8% pooled reference share vs 2.9%).

evidence.description: Critiques held roughly level from 2020 onward, mostly between 5 and 15 works per half year, while supportive works grew steadily and then sharply after 2023.
Fisher's exact test across 24-month pre/post windows yielded 28/114 critiques before vs 32/192 after (odds ratio 0.62, 95% CI 0.33 to 1.14, p = 0.10).
39 of 46 later critiques with at least five resolved references cited an earlier critique, against 180 of 321 later supportive works (odds ratio 4.35, 95% CI 1.85 to 11.88, p < 0.001).

17 of 58 later critiques matched an earlier critique author on surname and first initial, compared to 66 of 380 later supportive works matching an earlier supportive author (odds ratio 1.97, 95% CI 0.99 to 3.80, p = 0.046).
Examination of the Crossref funder field for all 2,032 records revealed zero critiques reporting Meta, Facebook, or Instagram support.
Minich and Moreno (2024), an EMA study finding adolescent smartphone use associated with better mood, was the sole record naming Facebook and was recoded N under verification rule R3.

Of resolved references in later critiques with at least 5 resolved references, 6.8% pointed to earlier critiques, compared to 2.9% of resolved references in later supportive works pointing to earlier critiques.

methodologies.name: Bibliometric citation and authorship continuity analysis
methodologies.description: Assembles a rule-defined corpus of works engaging the adolescent social media harm thesis, stance-codes them, and tests for changes in output share, citation continuity, and author continuity before versus after Meta's March 2023 meeting notes.
conditions: Corpus restricted to works from January 2017 to October 2026 meeting topic and engagement criteria
Exclusion of March 2023 as a boundary month
LLM stance coding blind to dates on first pass followed by rule-based verification

limitations.text: The bibliometric design cannot detect private contact, direct outreach to existing critics, editorial influence, or changes in tone.
All stance coding was performed by a large language model rather than human experts, and the verification pass used the same model family while seeing publication dates.
Coding works based on titles and abstracts misses positions and nuances stated only in the full body text.
191 works had no retrievable abstract and were coded from title alone under rule R4, pushing them toward a 'neither' classification.
Corpus boundaries missed some relevant critical works, capturing only 12 of 19 pre-listed check list critiques.
Reference data and Crossref funder metadata are incomplete across records, and recent months are undercounted due to indexing lag.
Author matching on surname and first initial may produce false matches and miss authors who changed names.
Statistical window tests had limited statistical power due to sample size (~300 stance works across 24-month windows) and cannot rule out a small rise in critique share.

future_work.text: Conduct an independent human check of stance coding on a stratified random sample of 150 works blind to period and model codes.
Score abstract and conclusion language strength across the March 2023 boundary for critics publishing in both periods to evaluate changes in rhetorical forcefulness.
